title: MCP Server
snippet:
Connect AI assistants to Front via the MCP server
Front's MCP server (`mcp.frontapp.com/mcp`) lets AI agents act on Front conversation data using a single OAuth-authenticated endpoint. Agents authenticate as a specific Front user, with permissions matching that user's role (user-scoped authorization). The MCP server is separate from the [Admin MCP server](https://dev.frontapp.com/docs/admin-mcp-server), which manages Front configurations such as rules, setting up teammates, managing AI features, etc.
This article covers how to connect the MCP server to any MCP-compatible client to Front using an OAuth app you create yourself in the Front developer settings. For the user-facing overview, official directory listings (Claude, and others coming), and use case inspirations for Front teammates, see the general [Help Center article on the MCP server](https://help.front.com/en/articles/4883136).

| | |
|---|---|
| **Endpoint** | `https://mcp.frontapp.com/mcp` |
| **Transport** | Streamable HTTP |
| **MCP spec version** | 2025-11-25 |
| **Auth** | OAuth 2.1 + PKCE compatibility **Note:** Front does not support Dynamic Client Registration. Your AI assistant must support a ***confidential connection that sends an OAuth client ID and secret***. Some popular AI assistants are currently not compatible. |
| **Identity model** | Per-user tokens. Every tool call attributes to a specific Front teammate |
| **Who can connect** | Any teammate |
| **Scopes** | `read`, `write`, `send` |
The identity model is the part most worth internalizing: the agent's effective permissions are exactly the authorizing teammate's permissions. If the teammate can't see an inbox, the agent can't either.
###
Incompatibility list
Some AI assistants do not support confidential connections. These clients cannot connect to the Front MCP server:
- Any client that requires Dynamic Client Registration (DCR)

> If you're using Claude or ChatGPT, we recommend you connect the Front MCP server from the official directories:
>
>
> - [Claude official directory](https://claude.ai/directory/connectors/front)
> - [ChatGPT official directory](https://chatgpt.com/plugins/plugin_asdk_app_6aaab462482c819183764e2f6a72e8e9)
>

Connecting an AI assistant to Front's MCP server has two general steps: create a Front developer app with the Front MCP feature, and then connect your AI client using the app's credentials.

title: Get started with Front's MCP server
snippet:
⚠️ **Front’s MCP server allows external AI tools (e.g., Claude, ChatGPT) to connect to Front.** If you’re looking to connect in the opposite direction and allow Front’s AI to connect an external tool, follow the steps for [MCP Connectors](/en/articles/4971328).
## Overview
Front's MCP server lets you and your teammates connect Front to AI assistants like Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini, and Microsoft Copilot. Once connected, the AI assistant can use your conversations, draft replies, leave internal comments, and take other actions on your behalf — all while respecting the user permissions set within Front.
Because Front handles every channel — email, SMS, chat, and more — in one place, the AI assistant gets the full context of a conversation: messages across all channels, internal comments, tag and assignment history, and rule actions, all in one timeline.
Head to Front Community to read the [official announcement](https://community.front.com/announcements-63/front-s-mcp-server-bring-front-into-your-ai-workflows-3958) and get the [starter guide](https://community.front.com/workflows-discussion-47/front-mcp-server-starter-guide-plug-and-play-prompts-3964) with ready-to-use templates for the MCP.
---
## What is the MCP server?
MCP (Model Context Protocol) is an open standard that lets AI assistants connect to external tools. The *MCP server* specifically enables external AI assistants and similar tools to access a predetermined set of Front data and actions. Connecting to the Front MCP server means the AI assistant can do things like search your inbox, read a thread, draft a reply, leave an internal comment, or tag a conversation — as you, with your permissions.
**Think of it as giving the AI assistant a key to Front that only works while you're authorized, and only does the things your role already allows.**

title: Frontend MCP Server
snippet:
# Frontend MCP Server
The Frontend MCP server gives agents access to the parts of a project they can’t reach from the sandbox: its [Frontend Cloud](/cloud/overview) database, its media library, its deploy logs and environment variable names, image and video generation, Frontend’s build skills, and the [services the project has connected](/mcp/integrations). Every project has it, enabled by default.
```
https://mcp.frontend.co/mcp
```
## How agents use it
Section titled “How agents use it”
Instead of loading every action as a separate tool, the server offers four tools that let an agent find and run what it needs:
| Tool | What it does |
|---|---|
| `search_tools` | Finds the tools for a task, such as “query the database” or “list the store’s products”, and returns their input schemas and whether each service is connected. |
| `get_tool_schemas` | Returns the description and input schema of tools by name. |
| `multi_execute_tool` | Runs up to 20 tools at once, each with its arguments, and returns one result per call. |
| `list_connections` | Shows which services are connected, and to which account. |
Tool names combine the toolkit and the action, like `QUERY_DATABASE` or `SHOPIFY_LIST_PRODUCTS`. The agent’s own approval settings decide which calls need your confirmation: `multi_execute_tool` is marked as able to change data, and the other three as read-only.
## Frontend tools
Section titled “Frontend tools”
Frontend’s own tools are always available, with no connection needed:
| Tool | What it does | Needs |
|---|---|---|
| `LIST_SKILLS`, `LOAD_SKILL` | List Frontend’s skills, instructions for building features like payments, a CMS, a database, a contact form or AI, and load one by name. | — |
| `GET_DATABASE_SCHEMA` | Lists the tables and columns of the project’s database. | The project’s [database](/cloud/database) |
| `QUERY_DATABASE` | Runs any SQL (SQLite dialect), including writes and schema changes, with optional parameters for `?` placeholders. | The project’s [database](/cloud/database) |
| `LIST_MEDIA`, `UPLOAD_MEDIA`, `DELETE_MEDIA` | List, upload (from a URL) and delete files in the project’s [media library](/cloud/storage). Returns each file’s public URL. | — |
| `GENERATE_IMAGE` | Generates or edits images from prompts, optionally with reference images, and saves them to the media library. | [OpenRouter](/integrations/openrouter) |
| `GENERATE_VIDEO` | Starts a video generation and returns a ticket. | [OpenRouter](/integrations/openrouter) |
|

title: MCP Server
snippet:
# MCP Server
Frontend exposes a [Model Context Protocol](https://modelcontextprotocol.io) (MCP) server so AI agents — Claude, Cursor, or any MCP-compatible client — can work with your projects directly: read and write files, run git and database operations, manage environment variables and domains, generate media, and publish.
## Endpoint
Section titled “Endpoint”
```
https://mcp.frontend.co/mcp
```
The server speaks the **streamable HTTP** transport. It runs on the core Frontend app, so `https://www.frontend.co/mcp` resolves to the same endpoint.
## Authentication
Section titled “Authentication”
The MCP server uses the same **team API key** as the REST API, sent as a Bearer token. Create one from **Team Settings → API Keys** (`/teams/{handle}/api-keys`). The key is team-scoped — it can reach any project the team owns.
There is no cookie or session auth. Configure your MCP client to send:
```
Authorization: Bearer <your-api-key>
```
## Connecting a client
Section titled “Connecting a client”
Most MCP clients accept a remote server URL and a header. Example configuration:
```
{ "mcpServers" : { "frontend" : { "url" : " https://mcp.frontend.co/mcp " , "headers" : { "Authorization" : " Bearer <your-api-key> " } } } }
```
To explore the server interactively, run the MCP Inspector against the same URL and header:
```
npx @modelcontextprotocol/inspector
```
## How it works
Section titled “How it works”
No project is selected when you connect. An agent first calls the **`projects`** tool to list or search the team’s projects, then passes the chosen `projectId` to every other tool. Access is authorized per call against the key’s team.
A quick `tools/list` check with curl:
```
curl -X POST https://mcp.frontend.co/mcp \ -H " Authorization: Bearer <your-api-key> " \ -H " Content-Type: application/json " \ -H " Accept: application/json, text/event-stream " \ -d ' {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"tools/list","params":{}} '
```
## Tools
Section titled “Tools”
| Tool | Description |
|---|---|
| `projects` | List or search the team’s projects; returns ids to use with the other tools |
| `readFiles` | Read specific project files by path |
| `writeFile` | Create or update a file (validated and formatted) |
| `editFile` | Replace exact lines in a file |
| `bash` | Run a shell command over the project files (offline: no network) |
| `git` | `log`, `commit`, `branch`, `merge`, `restore`, `push`, `pull`, `pr` |
| `database` | Run SQL and inspect the schema of the Frontend Clou

title: Get started with Front's Admin MCP server [open beta]
snippet:
- **This feature is in beta.** This article may require final changes before the feature is released to general availability (GA).
- **Front's Admin MCP server allows external AI tools (e.g., Claude, ChatGPT) to manage your Front settings.** To let an AI tool work with your conversations instead, see [Get started with Front's MCP server](https://help.front.com/en/articles/4883136). To let Front's AI connect to an external tool, follow the steps for [MCP Connectors](https://help.front.com/en/articles/4971328).
## Overview
Front's Admin MCP server lets Front admins connect AI assistants like Claude and ChatGPT to their Front settings. Once connected, the AI assistant can read how your Front instance is set up and create or edit rules, inboxes, tags, message templates, knowledge bases, AI agents, and more, from a request written in plain language.
Every change is made as the admin who connected, only within what their Front role allows, and shows in your [audit log](https://help.front.com/en/articles/2925696).

MCP (Model Context Protocol) is an open standard that lets AI assistants connect to external tools. The Admin MCP server gives an AI assistant a set of tools to read and change your Front configuration, the same work you would otherwise do in your settings one item at a time.
It is separate from Front's MCP server. The MCP server works with conversations on behalf of any teammate. The Admin MCP server works with your settings on behalf of an admin.
**Think of it as giving your AI assistant access to your Front settings, with your admin role as the limit: it can only change what you could change yourself.**

### Option 1: Official connector in your AI assistant's directory
The simplest path is to find Admin MCP in the connector directory of your AI assistant and connect in a few clicks.
If your AI assistant is managed by your company, as it often is in larger organizations, your IT or business systems team may need to allow the connector before it appears in your account. If you don't see it listed, that's the team to ask.
- **Claude** — is available in the [Claude connector directory](https://claude.ai/directory/front-admin).

### Custom connection (any MCP-compatible client)
If you're building your own internal agent, a company admin can create a private developer app in Front and use its credentials to connect.

title: MCP
snippet:
The [Model Context Protocol](https://modelcontextprotocol.io) (MCP) lets coding agents use tools from outside their sandbox. Every Frontend project comes with MCP servers already configured, and Frontend writes them into [Claude Code](/agents/claude-code), [Codex](/agents/codex) and [OpenCode](/agents/opencode) before each agent starts. You don’t install or configure anything. ([Pi](/agents/pi) doesn’t support MCP.)
## The project’s servers
Section titled “The project’s servers”
| Server | When it’s added | What agents can do with it |
|---|---|---|
| [Frontend](/mcp/frontend) | Always | Query the project’s database, manage its media library, generate images and videos, read deploy logs and load build skills, plus the tools for the [services the project connects](/mcp/integrations): Shopify, Stripe, Supabase, Figma and Contentful |
| GitHub | When the team connects [GitHub](/integrations/github) | GitHub’s official server: repositories, issues and pull requests |
| [Your own](/mcp/custom-servers) | When you add them in **Settings → MCP Servers** | Anything the server offers |
See and switch these servers on or off in **Settings → MCP Servers**.
## How servers authenticate
Section titled “How servers authenticate”
- **Frontend** uses the project’s Frontend API key, which every project has in its `FRONTEND_API_KEY` [environment variable](/features/environment-variables). The key identifies the project, so the server only ever acts on it. Connected services’ tools use the credentials from the project’s connections.
- **GitHub** uses the access token from the team’s connection. Frontend supplies a current token each time an agent starts.
- **Your own servers** can reference the project’s environment variables in their URL and headers, like `Bearer ${LINEAR_API_KEY}`.
Credentials stay in Frontend’s configuration; agents call the tools without ever handling the keys behind them.

The Frontend server is a regular remote MCP server, so you can also connect a local agent to it with the project’s API key. See [Frontend MCP Server](/mcp/frontend#connect-from-your-own-machine).
